definitions.explanation: Describes food or drink that has a sweet taste. Used especially for sake, wine, curry, and sauces to indicate the sweeter end of the flavor spectrum.
For dishes like curry, indicates a mild, non-spicy level. Japanese curry products are typically graded from sweet (甘口) through medium (中辛) to hot (辛口).

examples.japanese: この{日本酒|にほんしゅ}は{甘口|あまくち}で{飲|の}みやすい。
examples.english: This sake is sweet and easy to drink.

examples.japanese: {甘口|あまくち}の{白|しろ}ワインが{好|す}きです。
{甘口|あまくち}の{醤油|しょうゆ}は{九州|きゅうしゅう}で{特|とく}に{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Sweet soy sauce is especially popular in Kyushu.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}には{甘口|あまくち}のカレーを{作|つく}る。
examples.english: I make mild curry for the children.

examples.japanese: {辛|から}いのが{苦手|にがて}なので、いつも{甘口|あまくち}を{選|えら}ぶ。
examples.english: I'm not good with spicy food, so I always choose mild.

examples.japanese: このカレールーは{甘口|あまくち}・{中辛|ちゅうから}・{辛口|からくち}の{三種類|さんしゅるい}がある。
examples.english: This curry roux comes in three types: mild, medium, and hot.

notes:
USAGE:
Also functions as a の-adjective: {甘口|あまくち}の. Very common on food product labels and restaurant menus. The opposite is {辛口|からくち} (dry; spicy; hot).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甘口|あまくち}の{日本酒|にほんしゅ} (sweet sake)
- {甘口|あまくち}カレー (mild curry)
- {甘口|あまくち}ワイン (sweet wine)
- {甘口|あまくち}の{醤油|しょうゆ} (sweet soy sauce)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {辛口|からくち}: dry (for sake/wine); spicy/hot (for curry) — the opposite end of the flavor spectrum
- {中辛|ちゅうから}: medium spiciness — the middle grade, between {甘口|あまくち} and {辛口|からくち}
